minutes.headline: Parks Commission set 2021 beach day-pass prices and a rental policy, and put off the revolving fund switch for a year.
minutes.summary: The commission agreed to stay with the existing parks revolving account instead of converting it, after hearing conflicting legal views. It revised the town beach rental policy and voted a new day-pass structure for the 2021 season. It also discussed a proposed inspection and maintenance policy, Marshall Park ideas, and the open space committee's land review.

budget_items.topic: Parks revolving account (53D) balance and carryover
budget_items.what_was_said: A DOR attorney said a balance above the limit can be carried if reserved for a purpose, but that the existing balance cannot be moved to a different account type. The chair said the balance is currently over a figure in the thirty-thousands.
Interest on a 53D account should return to the account, but none has apparently ever been credited. Accounting will look into it.

budget_items.topic: Parks lines in the DPW budget
budget_items.what_was_said: A member saw for the first time that the salary lines plus care of parks make up the parks total under DPW.
The beach salary line has been overspent each year and is again over this year. Charging enough to recoup all lifeguard cost would price the town out of the market.
Beach revenue in 2019 did not cover the salaries. The town manager hopes swim lessons are self-funded.

Members settled on an hourly rental fee with a two-hour minimum and a non-refundable deposit credited to the bill. Lifeguard cost was discussed as separate, with an extra lifeguard per group-size threshold.
Voted day pass: a resident adult covers up to three children under fifteen, with a lower rate for seniors or extra children, and a higher non-resident rate.
figures_as_heard: five dollars for seniors or additional child

budget_items.what_was_said: Season passes stay as proposed for residents and non-residents, with an add-on for extra dependents.
A 20 percent add-on to vendor prices partly covers absorbed credit card fees and partly funds advertising.

decisions.decision: Hold off converting the 53D revolving account to a 53E½ account for now; revisit in about a year, and ask the accounting staff to join a future meeting.
Seasonal beach employment was reported approved for the requested dates.
Kayla and the chair will revise the beach rental policy and form for approval at the next meeting.
Members will send Marshall Park idea lists to Kayla to compile; the item is deferred to the next meeting.
Anna will draft an inspection and maintenance policy and work on it with Chris.
Next meeting set tentatively for Monday the 29th at 6:30, with the beach, Marshall Park and a first policy review on the agenda.
No cash at the beach this year; the issue can be revisited.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to approve a new beach day-pass price structure for the 2021 season, leaving season passes unchanged.
The commission agreed to hold off converting the parks revolving account from 53D to 53E½ for about a year and to ask accounting staff to join a future meeting.
Members settled on an hourly beach rental fee with a two-hour minimum and a non-refundable deposit; Kayla and the chair will revise the policy and form for approval next meeting.
Members said the beach salary line has been overspent each year and is over again this year; no cash will be taken at the beach this year.
Anna will draft a parks inspection and maintenance policy with Chris, and Marshall Park ideas were deferred to the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The day-pass structure voted here sets what residents and non-residents pay at the town beach in 2021, and the no-cash decision changes how they pay.
Beach revenue did not cover beach salaries in 2019 and the salary line is over budget again, so the part of lifeguard cost that fees do not cover falls to the town budget, which is mostly taxes.
Keeping the parks revolving account as it is means its balance and any uncredited interest stay open questions for another year.
watch_next: Next meeting, tentatively Monday the 29th at 6:30, with final approval of the beach rental policy and form, Marshall Park ideas and a first policy review on the agenda.
Accounting's check on whether interest was ever credited to the parks revolving account.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main outcomes: the 4-0 fee-structure vote, staying with the 53D, the rental rates, the pass prices and the next steps. Ours adds several figures and items the official minutes lack. A reader should check the scope of the vote: ours says only day-pass prices changed and season passes were left alone, but the official minutes accept a fee structure that includes individual and family pass rates.
